title: perf(canary): auto-detect latency/throughput regressions + rollout guards
author: Aisha Menon
release_notes: Add automatic performance regression detection for canaries; introduce hysteresis-based rollout guards to reduce noisy rollouts. Backwards compatible; opt-in via canary config.
body: Context: We've seen several incidents where small latency regressions in new model variants caused aggressive canary rollouts to escalate and trigger wider rollouts before the regression was detected. This PR implements an automated detector for latency and throughput regressions in perf canaries and couples it with rollout guards (hysteresis + minimum-sample checks) so rollouts are paused until regressions are resolved. Motivation: reduce blast radius from noisy metrics and false positives, make canary decisions deterministic, and surface clear signals for on-call. What this change does: 1) Adds a streaming detector that compares rolling-window p50/p95/p99 and throughput against baseline model variants using Welch's t-test + bootstrapped confidence intervals to detect regressions with configurable alpha. 2) Introduces hysteresis-based rollout guards: a candidate must pass N consecutive windows and not exceed regression thresholds before progression; failing windows increment a backoff timer that prevents auto-rollforward. 3) Implements minimum-sample enforcement and outlier trimming to avoid noisy windows during low traffic. 4) Adds a canary-config schema (canary.policy.autodetect.enabled, .alpha, .min_samples, .hysteresis_windows, .backoff_seconds) with defaults matching current product expectations. 5) Exposes detector diagnostic metrics and an explanation field in the canary UI and API for auditability. Design notes: - Detector runs in the perf-canary service as a separate analysis stage to avoid impacting request path. - We use incremental aggregation to keep memory linear with number of canaries and constant per-window cost. - Thresholds are conservative by default to prioritize availability; teams can tighten alpha. - Backward compatible: autodetect is opt-in per canary; existing behavior unchanged if disabled. Testing: - Unit tests for statistics and bootstrapping logic. - Integration test that replays historical canary traces including a known p95 regression (from ENG-3129) and verifies detector flags it and stops the rollout. - E2E smoke that exercises canary progression with the guard enabled. - Performance microbench for detector overhead (<1% CPU on perf-canary under 10k rps). Rollout plan: - Feature flag gated; enable for internal perf team canaries first (staging). - Monitor detector false-positive rate and rollout pauses for 2 weeks, then enable for broader customers. - If we observe unexpected pauses, we will revert via feature flag and open ENG follow-up. Backwards compatibility and migration: - Adds new config keys with safe defaults. - No changes required for existing canaries. Checklist: - [x] Tests added (unit/integration/e2e) - [x] Metrics and logs added - [x] Docs updated (canary policy + console) - [x] Linear tickets linked (ENG-3129, ENG-3290) - [x] Feature-flagged behind canary.autodetect.enabled Notes/risks: - Statistical detectors can still produce false positives under adversarial traffic patterns; we've added explanatory diagnostics to simplify on-call triage. - Threshold tuning might be required per workload; default settings are intentionally conservative. Related: perf-canary detector RFC, internal runbook link (docs/internal/perf/canary-detector).

review_thread: Liam Chen: Can you justify the choice of Welch's t-test over non-parametric tests? Concern about low-sample regimes.

Author (Aisha): Welch's t-test paired with bootstrapped CIs gives a good balance of sensitivity and speed; we additionally enforce min_samples and use percentile trimming to mitigate low-sample noise. Added note in code and docs.
Priya Kapoor: Please add a canary-config default that disables auto-rollforward for model-variant upgrades during region failover (safety).
Author: Added canary.policy.autodetect.disable_rollforward_during_failover and covered in tests.
